description: A single-panel figure consisting of one table only, presented without a panel letter and with no accompanying micrograph, curve or schematic. The table has six column headers reading exactly "Strip", "Fe", "Mn", "Al", "C" and "Be", separated from the data body by horizontal rules. Four data rows are labelled "0Be", "0.5Be", "1.0Be" and "1.5Be". In every row the Fe entry is printed as "Bal." (balance), while Mn is 30, Al is 10 and C is 1.5 — identical across all four strips. Only the Be column differs, reading 0, 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 in the order of the rows. No unit is printed inside the table image itself; the caption supplies "wt%". There are no other numbers, footnotes or graphics. The table therefore defines the four alloy variants compared throughout the paper: a single common Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C base composition varied only by beryllium addition level (0 to 1.5 wt%), so any property difference reported elsewhere in the study is attributable to the Be content alone.

observations.observation: The entire figure is a single table; there are no micrographs, spectra, curves or schematics.
The table headers are printed exactly as 'Strip', 'Fe', 'Mn', 'Al', 'C' and 'Be'.
Four data rows are labelled '0Be', '0.5Be', '1.0Be' and '1.5Be'.
Fe is given as 'Bal.' (balance) in every one of the four rows.
Mn is 30, Al is 10 and C is 1.5 in all four rows, i.e. these three elements do not vary between strips.
The Be column reads 0 for 0Be, 0.5 for 0.5Be, 1.0 for 1.0Be and 1.5 for 1.5Be, so Be is the only varying composition variable.
No unit string is printed inside the table image; the caption states the compositions are nominal and expressed in wt%.
The caption describes the tabulated materials as 'the studied steel strips in this study'.
The caption presents these values as nominal (target) compositions rather than measured chemical analysis.

subfigures.description: One unlabelled table with headers Strip, Fe, Mn, Al, C, Be and four rows (0Be, 0.5Be, 1.0Be, 1.5Be). Fe = 'Bal.' in all rows; Mn = 30, Al = 10, C = 1.5 in all rows; Be = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 respectively. No units printed in the image.
